finding.claim: wipe() ignores the boolean result of requireRole(), so any authenticated user can wipe any tenant
finding.source: Caller-supplied User u (roles from request auth) and tenant path parameter {t} (route comment at line 24)

trace.note: requireRole(User, String) returns boolean; javadoc at line 13 says it does not throw
Returns u.roles().contains(role) with no side effect
requireRole(u, "OWNER") called as a statement; return value discarded, so no check happens
repo.wipe(tenant) runs unconditionally for any caller and tenant

finding.guards_checked: Only role check is requireRole() at line 26, which is a no-op because its result is ignored. No tenant-ownership check. export() at line 32 uses checkRole(), which throws, confirming this is a bug. Precondition: any authenticated user, including one with no roles, reaches wipe() via the route at line 24.

verdict.guard_found: none. requireRole() at src/Admin.java:14-15 returns a boolean with no side effect, and the call at src/Admin.java:26 is a bare statement whose result is discarded. No other check sits before repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27, and no tenant-ownership check exists. A grep of the directory finds no route-level role annotation or filter for the /tenants/{t}/wipe route at line 24-25. checkRole() at lines 18-22 is the throwing variant, and export() at line 32 uses it correctly.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 discards the boolean from requireRole() (defined at src/Admin.java:14-15, which does not throw), so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated caller, including one with no roles, against any tenant. Nothing else in the directory enforces a role on that route.

finding.claim: export() checks the OWNER role but not that the requested tenant is one the caller belongs to, enabling cross-tenant data export by any tenant's OWNER
finding.source: Caller-supplied User u with OWNER role (record User at line 4 has no tenant field) and tenant path parameter {t} (route comment at line 30)

trace.note: User(name, roles) has no tenant identifier, so roles are global and not bound to a tenant
checkRole() throws SecurityException when the role is missing
checkRole(u, "OWNER") verifies role only; tenant argument never compared to the tenants the user is entitled to
repo.export(tenant) exports whatever tenant the caller named

finding.guards_checked: Role check at line 32 is effective (throws), unlike F1. No tenant-scoping check in export(). Finding depends on roles being global; if upstream auth restricts roles per tenant or Repo.export() enforces tenant membership, it is downgraded or invalid. Neither is visible in this code.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at src/Admin.java:18-21 throws when the role is missing, and it is called at line 32, so the OWNER check is effective. No tenant-membership check exists in export() (lines 31-34) or anywhere in the repo, which is the only file present.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate (User at Admin.java:4 has no tenant field, checkRole at line 32 checks role only, and repo.export(tenant) at line 33 uses the caller-supplied tenant), but whether an OWNER of one tenant can export another depends on how roles are assigned upstream, which is not in the repo; if OWNER is global by design the finding is invalid, and if it is tenant-scoped the export is a real cross-tenant gap.
